PART I

Item 1. Business

Overview

Acme Robotics, Inc. ("Acme," the "Company," "we," "us" or "our") designs, manufactures and services autonomous mobile robots for warehouses, hospitals and light manufacturing. We were incorporated in Delaware in 2011 and are headquartered in Columbus, Ohio. Our robots move inventory, carry medical supplies and tend machines on factory floors without fixed guide rails.

We operate in two reportable segments: Warehouse Automation, which sells and leases our Courier and Lift robot fleets to distribution centers, and Healthcare Logistics, which sells our MedRunner robots and the related fleet software to hospital systems. Recurring revenue from software subscriptions and service contracts represented 38% of total revenue in fiscal 2024, compared with 33% in fiscal 2023.

Customers

We sell to more than 640 customers in 19 countries. Our largest customer, a national grocery distributor, accounted for approximately 14% of total revenue in fiscal 2024. No other customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue.

Competition

The market for autonomous mobile robots is competitive and changing quickly. We compete with large industrial automation companies, with warehouse system integrators and with venture-funded robotics start-ups. We believe we compete favorably on navigation reliability, fleet software and total cost of ownership.

Human Capital

As of December 31, 2024, we had 2,310 full-time employees, of whom approximately 1,050 worked in engineering and research and development. None of our employees in the United States are represented by a labor union.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should consider carefully the risks described below.

We depend on a limited number of suppliers for lidar sensors and motor controllers.

Two suppliers provide substantially all of the lidar sensors used in our robots, and a single supplier in Taiwan provides our motor controllers. A disruption at any of these suppliers, including one caused by export controls, natural disasters or geopolitical tension, could delay our shipments for several quarters and increase our costs.

Our largest customer accounts for a significant share of our revenue.

Our largest customer accounted for approximately 14% of total revenue in fiscal 2024. If this customer reduces or delays its orders, our revenue and results of operations could be materially harmed.

Safety incidents involving our robots could harm our reputation.

Our robots operate near people. A collision or other safety incident could lead to product recalls, litigation, regulatory investigations and loss of customer confidence, even if the incident was not caused by a defect in our products.

Item 2. Properties

Our headquarters and main assembly plant are located in Columbus, Ohio, in a 410,000 square foot facility that we own. We lease engineering offices in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and Munich, Germany, and a refurbishment center in Reno, Nevada.

PART II

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

The following discussion should be read together with our consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Our fiscal year ends on December 31.

Overview of Fiscal 2024

Fiscal 2024 was a year of strong growth for Acme. Demand from grocery and general merchandise distribution centers remained high throughout the year as customers continued to automate picking and replenishment in response to persistent labor shortages. In Healthcare Logistics, we completed our largest deployment to date, a 120-robot MedRunner fleet across a seven-hospital system in the Midwest. We also introduced Lift 2, a heavier-payload robot for pallet movement, which began shipping in the third quarter.

Gross margin improved as a larger share of our revenue came from software subscriptions and service contracts, and as component costs for lidar sensors declined. Operating expenses grew more slowly than revenue, reflecting the scale of our engineering organization and lower spending on trade shows. We continued to invest in navigation software, fleet orchestration and our refurbishment program, which extends the useful life of leased robots returned at the end of their contract terms.

Supply conditions for motor controllers remained tight during the first half of the year. We qualified a second source for one controller model in the fourth quarter, but we still rely on a single supplier for most units. Our backlog of signed but undelivered robot orders was $412.6 million at December 31, 2024, compared with $298.0 million a year earlier.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

As of December 31, 2024, we had cash and cash equivalents of $618.4 million and an undrawn $300.0 million revolving credit facility. We believe these resources will be sufficient to fund our operations for at least the next 12 months. Capital expenditures were $88.5 million in fiscal 2024, primarily for the expansion of our Columbus assembly plant.

Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

We are exposed to foreign currency risk, primarily from euro-denominated revenue in Europe, which represented approximately 11% of total revenue in fiscal 2024. A hypothetical 10% change in the euro to U.S. dollar exchange rate would have changed revenue by approximately $17 million.
